newsitem.title: INDIA: UK's Major sticks up for endangered tigers.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major sticks up for endangered tigers.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major, described by a political opponent as an endangered species, called on Thursday for greater protection of the threatened Indian tiger.
Major, on the first day of week-long visit to South Asia, told Indian businessmen in Calcutta that he regretted the tiger had become one of the most endangered animals in the world.
"The plight of the tiger is close to the hearts of the British people, and is of concern the world over," Major told some 6,000 business leaders.

Major, who surprised some senior Conservative party members by travelling abroad so close to a general election due in no more than four months, said he welcomed steps India was taking to shield the tiger from extinction.
"More needs to be done," Major said. "The tiger is a proud and glorious animal. We must ensure his survival so that our great grandchildren can enjoy his grace and power as much as we do."
According to the London-based Environmental Investigation Agency (EIA), poachers seeking tiger bones used in Chinese medicine are killing at least one Indian Bengal tiger a day.
EIA estimates the Indian tiger population at 2,500, and says the animal is threatened with extinction.
Tony Banks, a Labour Party member of parliament and an animal rights campaigner, has described Major, trailing the opposition by some 20 points in opinion polls, as an endangered species.
